issues.failure_explanation: The proof has just shown that $\mathcal{G}' = \{\psi_j^+\}_{j\in\mathcal{I}_1\cup\mathcal{I}_2'}\cup\{\psi_j^-\}\cup\{w^{-j}\}_{j=1}^k$ is a frame for $L_2(\gamma)$, and then infers that $\Span\{\psi_j^+\}_{j\in\mathcal{I}_1\cup\mathcal{I}_2'}$ is dense in $L_2^+(\gamma)$ merely because $\psi_j^+\in L_2^+$ while $\psi_j^-,w^{-j}\in L_2^-$. That inference requires $(f,\psi_j^-)=0$ for $f\in L_2^+$, i.e., sesquilinear orthogonality $L_2^+\perp L_2^-$. But the Hardy projections are oblique in general: the Cauchy Riesz projection on a non-circular Lipschitz curve is not self-adjoint, so $L_2^+\not\perp L_2^-$ (e.g., on $\gamma=\{(2+\cos\theta)e^{i\theta}\}$, $(w,w^{-1})=\int_\gamma e^{2i\theta}|w'(\theta)|\,d\theta\neq 0$ with $w\in L_2^+$, $w^{-1}\in L_2^-$). Hence the density claim is unproven as written. The claim itself is true and follows in one line from Lemma lem:frames_under_closed_range_mappings(i) applied to the frame $\mathcal{G}'$ with $T=P^+$ (then $P^+\psi_j^+=\psi_j^+$ and $P^+\psi_j^-=P^+w^{-j}=0$), and similarly with $P^-$ for the negative part.

failure_location.quote: Since $\psi_j^+ \in L^+_2(\gamma)$ while $\psi_j^-, w^{-j} \in L^-_2(\gamma)$, this implies in particular that $\Span\{\psi^+_j\}_{j \in \I_1\cup\I_2'}$ is dense in $L^+_2(\gamma)$, and that $\Span(\{\psi^-_j\}_{j =1}^\infty \cup \{w^{-j}\}_{j = 1}^k)$ is dense in $L^-_2(\gamma)$; hence $\Span(\{\psi^+_j\}_{j \in \I_1} \cup \{\psi^-_j\}_{\N \setminus \J} \cup \{w^{-j}\}_{j = 1}^k)$ is dense in $L_2(\gamma)$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the missing argument: apply Lemma lem:frames_under_closed_range_mappings(i) to the frame $\mathcal{G}'$ with the bounded closed-range projections $T=P^+$ and $T=P^-$ to obtain that $\{\psi_j^+\}_{j\in\mathcal{I}_1\cup\mathcal{I}_2'}$ is a frame for $L_2^+(\gamma)$ and $\{\psi_j^-\}\cup\{w^{-j}\}$ is a frame for $L_2^-(\gamma)$; the rest of the proof is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The removal lemma's conclusion lacks a complete proof at the density step; since the case $\delta<\infty$ of thm:lusin_frame is deduced from this lemma, that case is unsupported until the step is repaired. The lemma's statement itself is true.
issues.title: Removal lemma deduces Hardy-subspace density from a frame via false orthogonality
issues.why_classification: A single invalid inference with a one-line repair available from a lemma already proved and used elsewhere in the paper; no statement, rate, regime, or downstream guarantee changes, so the issue is minor.

issues.failure_explanation: The corollary is proved by applying Theorem thm:abstract_sfe (thm:abstract_sfe-2) with $h(\lambda) = \lambda^k(e^{-\lambda}\chi^+(\lambda) + e^{\lambda}\chi^-(\lambda))$. This symbol does not satisfy the theorem's decay hypothesis for any $\alpha > 0$: for $\lambda = 1+iy$, $y\to\infty$ (which lies in $S_\mu^o$ and has $\chi^+(\lambda)=1$), $|h(\lambda)| = |\lambda|^k e^{-\Re\lambda} \simeq y^k$ grows polynomially, while the required bound $|\lambda|^\alpha(1+|\lambda|)^{-2\alpha} \simeq y^{-\alpha}$ decays to $0$. The commented-out proof even asserts 'Clearly this choice of $h$ satisfies the conditions of Theorem thm:abstract_sfe', which is false. Thus the corollary is unsupported as written (its statement is nevertheless the correct standard square function estimate, e.g., an equality on the unit disk), and every result proved from it loses its proof support.

failure_location.quote: This follows by applying Theorem~\ref{thm:abstract_sfe} with the symbol $h(\lambda) = \lambda^k\big(e^{-\lambda}\chi^+(\lambda) + e^{\lambda}\chi^-(\lambda)\big)$, using the fact that $BD f_t = -\partial_t f_t$, and then doing the change of variables $z = r_\gamma(\theta)e^{-t}e^{i\theta}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the hypothesis of Theorem thm:abstract_sfe so that it covers the symbols $\lambda^k e^{\mp\lambda}\chi^\pm$ used here (the estimate is cited as a special case of Auscher--Ros\'en, whose actual hypothesis accommodates such symbols), or insert a short approximation lemma extending the square function estimate to symbols with polynomial growth and exponential decay off the imaginary axis (e.g., by truncating the symbol and using the convergence lemma lem:convergence_lemma). No conclusion needs to change.
issues.overall_effect: Theorem thm:square_function_estimates-1 is proved from this corollary; it in turn is the engine behind thm:lusin_frame (the discretization step), prop:frames_for_hardy_spaces, and the non-vanishing arguments in prop:no_lusin_basis. Until the invocation is repaired, the proof chain for the paper's central frame theorem is incomplete, though the stated estimates are the true standard ones.
issues.title: Square-function corollary applies the abstract SFE with a symbol violating its decay hypothesis
issues.why_classification: A cited theorem is applied outside its stated hypotheses at the paper's central technical step, and the source supports no purely cosmetic fix: either the abstract theorem's hypothesis must be corrected to match the cited result or a new approximation argument must be supplied. This is a contained repair with no loss of conclusions, but it is more than a routine local fix, so the issue is moderate.
